question: Does explicit within-frame integration of a bounded gate-weave trajectory reproduce analytic shutter blur more faithfully than the retained instantaneous end-of-frame sampler without chained resampling or range escape?

controls.instantaneous: sample the immutable source once at the current frame offset
controls.analytic_truth: closed-form temporal mean of the same sinusoidal chart along the linear prior-to-current offset segment
controls.dense_reference: 256 midpoint samples from the immutable source
controls.static_trajectory: equal start and end offsets must equal the retained bilinear sampler exactly

forbidden: resample an already shifted prior frame
infer shutter duration, transport mechanics or rolling shutter from image content
change trajectory, sample counts, chart, controls or gates after formal scoring
claim synthetic shutter integration is measured scanner, projector, camera or stock behaviour

branch_rule.pass: retain bounded midpoint shutter integration as an optional generic physical-inspired gate-weave sampling mode and next measure streamed sequence cost
branch_rule.fail: retain instantaneous immutable-source sampling and close within-frame integration without sample-count or gate rescue

claim_ceiling: Synthetic within-frame translation-integration accuracy only; not measured film transport, shutter, scanner, projector, camera, video quality, stock calibration or product readiness.
